text: dsh-zai-usage 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 Z.AI Coding Plan 配额面板。插件通过 DSH bundle 将面板加入侧栏；主进程定期调用 Z.AI 接口读取配额窗口、工具调用用量和订阅计划，并把快照写入 DSH home，客户端读取快照显示剩余额度、已用量、重置时间与计划名称，也可手动刷新。适合需要在 DSH 中查看 Z.AI Coding Plan 用量的人。需要配置可由 DSH credentials 服务解析的 ZAI_API_KEY。

dsh-zai-usage adds a Z.AI Coding Plan panel to the DSH web sidebar. It periodically fetches quota and subscription details from Z.AI, saves a snapshot in the DSH home directory, and displays usage, remaining quota, reset times, and plan name. Configure ZAI_API_KEY through DSH credentials.
想在 DSH 侧栏查看 Z.AI Coding Plan 还剩多少配额？
我想同时看到 Z.AI 的工具调用额度和重置时间。
How can I check my Z.AI coding plan quota from the DSH sidebar?
dsh-zai-usage 的功能「配额与订阅用量展示」：服务端定期读取 Z.AI 配额窗口和有效订阅信息，客户端以进度条显示剩余比例、已用数量、额度上限及重置时间。
dsh-zai-usage 的功能「手动刷新配额快照」：用户可在侧栏点击 Refresh，客户端重新读取最新快照并更新配额和计划信息。
dsh-zai-usage 使用前须知：需要由 DSH credential service 解析 ZAI_API_KEY，并将带 Bearer 认证的配额与订阅请求发送至 api.z.ai。

dsh-zai-usage README · dsh-zai-usage：Z.AI coding-plan quota panel in the DSH sidebar.

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin,
packaged as a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and
`cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `zai-usage` row into the active profile.
The client half is served from `lib/client.js` (`dsh.client.platform: web`).

dsh-zai-usage README · Install：- Desktop app: **Plugins** → install `github:bosenok/dsh-zai-usage` (private repository:
  give the machine git access), then enable the bundle.
- CLI: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:bosenok/dsh-zai-usage`.
- Local checkout: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:/path/to/dsh-zai-usage`.

Enabling the bundle mounts the plugin; HMR applies it to a running app, and a
restart makes sure the client half is rebuilt.

dsh-zai-usage README · Install：> Note for the app-managed `desktop` profile: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add`
> only installs the dependency and copies the package; unlike a regular profile
> it does not enable the bundle. Enable it by adding the package name to
> `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json` (or through the
> Plugins page). Other profiles enable the installed bundle automatically.

dsh-zai-usage README · Where the key comes from：The host half declares `inject: ['credentials']` and resolves the key through the
harness credential service — the same canonical seam the Z.AI provider itself
uses:

```js
const resolved = await ctx.credentials.resolve('ZAI_API_KEY')
```

dsh-zai-usage README · Where the key comes from：So there is nothing plugin-specific to configure. The value is found in the
service's layers: the credential store written when the Z.AI provider is
configured (`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` → `refs`), or the environment layers
(`~/.dsh/.env`, inherited environment, the project's `.env`). The value never
reaches the browser: the client half renders the quota snapshot only.

dsh-zai-usage README · Where the key comes from：Missing key: the panel shows `ZAI_API_KEY is not set in the credential store`, and
the snapshot `~/.dsh/usage/zai-usage.json` carries `debug` with the resolution
state (`credsService`, `resolve`) — for instance
`{"credsService":"ok","resolve":"value(49) source=file"}`.

dsh-zai-usage README · Versioning：This project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`).
Releases are tagged in git (`v0.1.0` and later `v0.1.x` tags), announced
as GitHub releases and documented in [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md).

`engines.dsh` in `package.json` pins the compatible DSH range.

Bump policy: **patch** — fixes; **minor** — new features without breaking the
configuration; **major** — breaking changes to the configuration, the session
format or the supported DSH range.

dsh-zai-usage README · Versioning：`CHANGELOG.md` is generated with [git-cliff](https://git-cliff.org/) from
[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`cliff.toml`):

```sh
./scripts/changelog.sh                 # print unreleased notes
./scripts/changelog.sh v0.2.0          # add the next release section
git cliff -o CHANGELOG.md              # full regeneration (curated history is kept otherwise)
```

To install a specific release instead of a moving branch, pin the tag:

dsh-zai-usage README · Versioning：```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "git+ssh://git@github.com/bosenok/dsh-zai-usage.git#v0.1.0"
```

Tags are created on `master` by Git Flow; integration builds live on `develop`
(install with `#develop` if you want the latest unreleased code).

dsh-zai-usage README · Development：`lib/` is built and committed; the sources live in `src/`. Rebuild the client with
the repository's Vite config (`npx vite build` → `dist/`, then the wrapper in
`build/wrapper.js` produces `lib/client.js`).

dsh-zai-usage README · License：MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party code bundled into `lib/` and its
licenses are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

dsh-zai-usage README · Git Flow：Development follows [Git Flow](https://github.com/git-flow/git-flow-next) via the
committable `.gitflow` configuration. In a fresh clone activate it once:

```sh
./scripts/gitflow-setup.sh
```

(The script runs `git flow config sync` and creates the local `master`/`develop`
branches. `git flow config sync` alone is enough if both base branches already
exist.)

dsh-zai-usage README · Git Flow：| Branch | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `master` | released code only; every commit here is tagged `vX.Y.Z` |
| `develop` | integration branch (repository default branch) |
| `feature/*` | one change, started from and finished into `develop` |
| `release/*` | stabilization, started from `develop`, finished into `master` + `develop` |
| `hotfix/*` | urgent production fix, started from `master`, finished into both |

```sh
git flow feature start my-change
